        <h1 class="academic-section-title">Biography</h1>

        <p>I am a Discovery Postdoc in computational and systems biology at <strong>Novartis Biomedical Research</strong> in Basel, Switzerland. In my current work, I apply bulk and single-cell RNA-seq alongside SomaScan proteomics to correlate molecular profiles with clinical outcomes. I collaborate closely with multidisciplinary teams to investigate the mechanisms and biomarkers of tendinopathy, osteoarthritis, and tissue regeneration using statistical modeling, machine learning, and bioimaging approaches.</p>

        <p>Previously, I was a Postdoctoral Researcher in the Department of Biomedicine at the <strong>University of Basel / University Hospital Basel</strong> (2023–2024), where I studied the gut-liver axis in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD), performing scRNA-seq analyses of mucosal-associated innate-like T cells, multivariate modeling of patient microbiota dynamics, and bioimage quantification of intestinal barrier integrity. I earned my Ph.D. in Cell and Systems Biology at the <strong>University of Zurich</strong> (2017–2022) in the group of Prof. Erik C. Böttger, investigating how ribosomal mistranslation shapes proteostasis, ER stress, and mitochondrial function via transcriptomics, metabolomics, and fluorescence microscopy.</p>

        <p>My core passion is transforming complex clinical and biological data into actionable insights through exploratory data analysis, rigorous hypothesis testing, and interactive data visualization (R/Bioconductor, Python, UNIX/HPC, Quarto, Shiny). Outside of research, I enjoy playing guitar, practicing yoga daily, mountain hiking, climbing, and participating in Toastmasters and the local Ski and Mountain club.</p>
